invoke_blocker: AccessDeniedException on every model: 'not authorized to perform the required AWS Marketplace actions (aws-marketplace:ViewSubscriptions, aws-marketplace:Subscribe)'. Listing works, invoking does not. Fix by enabling model access in the Bedrock console (admin, one-time) or adding aws-marketplace actions to the permission set. See docs/05-aws-services.md.
note: Model bindings live here, not in phase code. A phase asks for a tier; this file decides which model serves it. Swapping a model is editing this file. 'verified' below means an actual invoke succeeded -- set it only from a passing `python -m bedrock.verify` run, never from a report.

fast.purpose: Narration of already-computed facts. Discovery summaries, provisioning status, load progress, report prose. No judgement.

reasoning.purpose: Judgement under ambiguity. Root cause analysis, remediation SQL, edition rationale, cutover brief.

policy.no_opus_tier: Sonnet 4.5 serves every reasoning task, including work an Opus-class model could do. There is deliberately no third tier: the architecture dropped the frontier tier when PL/SQL conversion left scope, and a homogeneous Oracle-to-Oracle migration has no task that needs one. Opus profiles are available on this account (global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5 through opus-5) but are not bound -- reaching for one is a cost decision that needs justifying, not a default.
policy.both_tiers_use_profiles: ap-south-1 carries no on-demand throughput for current-generation models, so both tiers bind a global.* inference profile rather than a bare model id. A bare id returns a ValidationException that reads like a permissions error but is routing.

reasoning_apac.note: APAC-scoped Sonnet 4. Use when data residency requires the request stay in-region rather than routing globally.

fast_legacy.note: Claude 3 Haiku. Roughly a quarter the token cost of Haiku 4.5 and callable as a bare model id. Fall back to this only if fast-tier spend becomes the binding budget constraint -- see docs/06-cost-model.md.
